My go-to transcription tool on Mac, MacWhisper, today rolls out another major update, adding live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and brand-new transcription models. Here are the details.

MacWhisper's Apple Intelligence integration goes deeper

I've written in the past about how much I rely on MacWhisper, especially as part of my podcasting workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first AI-powered transcription tools on Mac. Since launching in 2023 by indie developer Jordi Bruin, it has continued to improve and expand support for new models, services and workflows.

These include automatic meeting recording, speaker identification, folder watching, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, as well as integration with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper updates to version 15.2, introducing improved speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was only announced a few hours ago.

This brings us to another major feature in this update: live meeting transcription.

This feature has sat near the top of MacWhisper's public roadmap for a while, and it's finally officially launching now, letting users follow along, scroll through, copy, or send live transcripts while a meeting is in progress.

As for the actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, supporting 22 languages, and further enhances integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Now, macOS users (including those in the EU) can search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, pull their contents into Shortcuts, and reference the transcript on the current screen in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organising transcripts and meetings, and supports dragging existing transcript files in from the sidebar.
